MINUTES
  Regular Meeting of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, November 16, 2021

In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 virus, Governor Newsom has signed Assembly
Bill 361. Please be advised that the Council Chambers are closed to the public and that some,
or all, of the Gardena City Council Members may attend this meeting telephonically.

The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of Gardena,
California, was called to order via Zoom at 7:03 p.m. on Tuesday, November 16, 2021, Mayor
Tasha Cerda presiding.

1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tern Rodney G. Tanaka; Council Member Mark E.
  Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; and Council Member Paulette C. Francis. Other
  City Officials and Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City Attorney Carmen
  Vasquez; and City Clerk Mina Semenza.

  At 7:04 p.m., the City Council recessed into Closed Session via Microsoft Teams, with the
  following in attendance: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tern Rodney G. Tanaka; Council
  Member Mark E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; Council Member Paulette C.
  Francis. Other City Officials and Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City
  Attorney Carmen Vasquez; and Directors Ray Beeman and Ernie Crespo.

 11. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES

  11.A Approval of Update to Guidelines for the Cares Act Program Funding (CDBG- CV)
  received from the US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to
  Alleviate the Negative Economic Impacts of Covid-19

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.
  Administrative Analyst Mary Simonell gave a PowerPoint Presentation.
  There were a number of questions and concerns from our Council regarding: the
  number of applications we approved and denied; the amount we gave out to our
  residents and businesses for rental assistance and for what time period; how
  small businesses were notified and what the HUD requirements were; if people
  are aware of the utility and nutrition program and possibly get the information out
  through our public schools, if the funds must be expended by September 2027; if
  the assistance is a one-time application program, and if we have money for the
  CDBG projects for improving infrastructure and eliminating blight, which Ms.
  Simonell answered. City Attorney Vasquez mentioned that the state had a
  program that had a greater amount of money that was paying back rent that the
  City hosted and that may be the reason why we have a balance in our fund.

  It was moved by Council Member Francis, seconded by Mayor Pro Tern Tanaka,
  and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve Guideline Updates:

  Ayes:  Council Member Francis, Mayor Pro Tern Tanaka, and Council
  Members Henderson, Kaskanian, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

   City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Senior Planner John Signo gave a PowerPoint presentation. The Applicant, Romain
  Bianchi of Lab 5, also gave a presentation.

  Mayor Cerda opened the Public Hearing at 9:54 p.m. and asked if there were any
  comments from the public. Being that there was none, she asked if Council had any
  comments.

  There was a number of questions and concerns from our Mayor and Council
  regarding storm water run-off, the noise study that was done, the amount of handicap
  parking spaces, alcohol permits and parking on site. Starla Barker, Consultant from
  DeNovo Planning came into the meeting to speak on the noise study. Mr. Bianchi,
  along with Assistant City Attorney Kranitz, answered all of Council's questions.

  There was no further comment; Mayor Cerda closed the Public Hearing at 10:48 p.m.

  It was moved by Mayor Pro Tern Tanaka, seconded by Council Member Francis,
  and carried by the following roll call vote to Adopt Resolution No. 6536:

  Ayes:  Mayor Pro Tern Tanaka and Council Members Francis, Henderson,
  Kaskanian, and Mayor Cerda

  Absent: None

21. COUNCIL REMARKS

  1. COUNCIL MEMBER FRANCIS - Since the last meeting Council Member Francis

  Cup, Aquatics Senior Center Community Outreach Meeting and Los Angeles County
  Central Committee Meeting. Council Member Francis shared that November is Native
  American Heritage Month. Reminded everyone on supporting small businesses and
  encouraged everyone to keep wearing a mask, wash hands, and continue to social
  distance to fight COVID-19. Lastly, wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving.

  2. MAYOR PRO TEM TANAKA- Since the last meeting Mayor Pro Tern Tanaka attended

   Council Meeting on Saturday. Mayor Pro Tern thanked Director Ernie Crespo and

  3. COUNCIL MEMBER KASKANIAN - Since the last meeting Council Member
  Kaskanian attended the City Employee Halloween Costume Contest, Halloween
  events at the parks, Veterans Day Ceremony, and third annual memorial of fallen
  officer Toshia Hirai.

  4. MAYOR CERDA- Since the last meeting Mayor Cerda attended, Los Angeles County
  City Selection Committee Meeting via Zoom, Color run event at City Hall, City
  Employee Costume Contest, Special Study Session, Halloween events at the parks
  and Ministerial lunch. Mayor Cerda shared she took a picture with Glen Mitchell a
  Rotary Club member to be posted on the Gardena Valley News. She also attended
  the graduation of the new Gardena Police Department recruits and congratulated
  them. Mayor Cerda shared her experience with GTrans in Orlando and is looking
  forward to more awards. Also attended a zoom meeting with the PTO of Serra High
  School, Eddy Awards, Veterans Day Ceremony, Memorial for Toshia Hirai, grand
  opening for the new salad restaurant. Lastly shared the Senior Health Fair.

  5. COUNCIL MEMBER HENDERSON - Stated that we shall continue to keep Toshia
  Hirai family in prayer, especially his young son. He attended most of the events that
  were mentioned by the other Council Members. He gave thanks and recognition to the
  City staff that we have because they work really hard for our community and for us -

  that identify underserved areas in our community. He is also looking towards 2022 so
  we can start figuring out what our equity objective will be to serve our community at a
  higher capacity.
